isolation: Exported SVO commit snapshot; unrelated uncommitted Uniform changes excluded. One GPU process at a time under repository lease; browser GPU paused.
scope: Opaque scenery renderer GPU span. Excludes running fluid solver, water extraction/optics, final composite, and app presentation. Not a complete wet-frame speedup claim.
method: 12 warmups; 12 stationary or 24 moving timestamp samples plus separate uninstrumented submit/fence samples; two repetitions per camera. Frames retain full-resolution primary geometry and material shading. Both arms use published voxel-face mesh, AO and shadows, GI off.
conclusions: Existing opt-in RASTER + AO already supports voxel faces; no additional production switch is required.
At depth 1, RASTER + AO reduces stationary GPU spans about 39-40% and moving spans about 34-41%. The 50% reduction target is not achieved.
All six A/B captures retain identical depth alpha at every pixel; silhouettes and water-sort depth are unchanged.

Appearance is changed: cast shadows are more defined, and broad/offscreen occlusion is absent. About 20-26% of stationary depth-1 pixels differ by more than 8/255 in at least one display channel. These measure appearance differences, not ground-truth error.
Voxel CONES already reuse world-space lighting records. Their per-pixel lattice key/lookup work remains a significant cost, unlike the smooth screen-lighting path.

The cached-shadow preview still spends on primary geometry, half-resolution horizon AO/shadow filtering, and full-resolution deferred shading. Turning visibility off entirely still costs about 2.6-2.7 ms at depth 0.
An isolated single-sun shader prototype removed the secondary-light exact-shadow branch. Gains were small/inconsistent and did not reach the target; discarded without changing production.

nextArchitecturalExperiment.approach: Persistent per-surface lighting storage directly addressed from voxel mesh faces; cached AO and sun visibility, retaining full-resolution material/specular evaluation.
nextArchitecturalExperiment.reason: Avoid per-frame screen-wide hash requests and repeated AO evaluation while keeping offscreen occlusion available.
requirements: Sample large greedy quads with a surface atlas; one value per merged face loses local shadows.
Invalidate on mesh, light, AO tuning and occluder changes; never reuse stale visibility during edits.
Budget construction and memory, including high refinement, and validate steady movement, disocclusion and cold/update frames.
Compare image quality and complete wet-frame GPU cost before claiming 2x.
nextArchitecturalExperiment.status: Design hypothesis only. No implementation or 2x result claimed.
